items.description: One fact from the code that the decisions rest on, as one short sentence under 20 words, then one path:line citation.

platform.description: Where each affected repo deploys, or "Unknown: no deploy config in the repo".

items.description: A file or doc that shows how a repo deploys.
One concrete deploy step this ticket adds, on that platform.
A deploy, server, credential or access fact the developer must settle before the sprint starts, and who can answer it. Never repeated in open_questions.
One thing the developer marked as unsure, and what the code says about it.
Something the approach leaves out without saying so, written as what to add.

question.description: One short line, under 20 words, ending in a question mark. No code tour; at most one path:line.

items.description: A few words; does not repeat the question.

options.description: Two to four choices the developer picks from; empty only when no choice fits.

recommended.description: The recommended option, copied exactly from options; the suggested answer when options is empty.

evidence.description: Indexes into findings (0-based) of the findings this question rests on; empty when none do.

items.description: What this option leads to, in under 15 words, written evenly with the others.

consequences.description: One line per option, in the same order as options; empty when options is empty.

reopens.description: Index into the earlier decisions this question reopens because the code shows a risk in it; -1 when it reopens none.

quote.description: The ticket's own words this decision serves, verbatim, at most 25 words; empty when source is none.

source.description: Where the quote is; none when the ticket does not ask for this.

ref.description: The comment's author, or the linked or epic ticket's key; empty otherwise.

anchor.description: Where in the ticket this decision comes from.

open_questions.description: Decisions the build needs, and product, scope or behaviour questions. Never about deploy, servers, credentials or access; those are deployment blockers.
